title: Add browser password login through the existing session

evidence: Fresh verifier-owned disposable SvelteKit action/SSR probe passed 1 file / 1 test: normalized pre-created scrypt credential, exact persisted Admin, common timingSafeEqual denial path, identical generic 401 body with no cookie/session, existing foundation_session attributes, /admin redirect and protected entry, separate logout/revocation denial, both provider starts, UI/form exports, owner boundary, and non-goals.

Fresh provider/session regression passed 2 files / 18 tests; npm run check passed with 0 errors/warnings; npm run test passed 28 files / 112 tests; npm run build and git diff --check passed. No execute receipt was reused and executor RED/GREEN remained supporting-only.

Fresh disposable hostile probe passed 1 file / 2 tests: dummy known-password integrity, malformed-credential closed denial, one scrypt derivation and shared timingSafeEqual path per denial, fresh tokens over a preexisting cookie, distinct concurrent sessions, current-session logout, persisted-role routing, HTTP/HTTPS cookie semantics, provider callback coexistence, and absence of password/provider secrets from the client build.

Focused password/session/invitation/Telegram/Google regression passed 4 files / 23 tests and git diff --check passed. Diff and boundary review admitted no material auth bypass, account enumeration, second auth lifecycle, provider regression, scope creep, or unjustified helper maintenance cost.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-011 / REQ-001 / REQ-014 RED: /login cannot verify a pre-created password credential or issue the existing server session; GREEN: disposable credential and HTTP/SSR probes prove normalized-email password success, scrypt/timingSafeEqual verification, externally identical invalid-credential denial without a session, existing cookie/Admin redirect, logout/revocation, and unchanged provider login paths; artifact: .tasks/TASK-030-T3-FT-001-W14/ and .protocols/TASK-030-T3-FT-001-W14/.
purpose: Allow a password-credential account to authenticate in the browser while reusing the existing server session/cookie and preserving provider login compatibility.
success_outcome: A pre-created password credential can authenticate through /login into the existing revocable server session and permitted context, while unknown email and wrong password are generic, timing-safe, and sessionless.
anti_goals: Do not implement or re-prove CLI bootstrap/account+credential creation; TASK-029 owns that dependency outcome.
Do not add self-registration, password reset/recovery, email verification, MFA, password history, password management UI, or a new dependency.
Do not remove or materially change Telegram/Google provider flows.
Do not add a new session token, cookie, authentication state store, role selector, or client-owned authorization context.

stop_conditions: Stop if implementation requires a new dependency, service, session/cookie type, durable auth-state store, provider removal, account-registration/recovery lifecycle, or accepted ownership-graph change.
Stop if route code would write credential/session tables directly, trust client role/account/center input, expose account existence, or persist/log plaintext password.
Stop if unknown email and wrong password cannot use one externally indistinguishable generic denial and the same timing-safe comparison path.

constraints: Identity & Access owns password verification and session issuance; SvelteKit login adapts form data and sets the existing cookie without direct persistence.
Normalize submitted email exactly with trim().toLowerCase() before lookup.
Use Node built-in scrypt derivation plus timingSafeEqual verification and add no dependency.
Reuse foundation_session cookie attributes, actor resolution, protected redirects, logout, and revocation behavior.
invariants: Unknown email and wrong password are externally indistinguishable, issue no session, and use the same timing-safe comparison path.
Successful password login grants only the persisted account role and creates the existing session type/cookie.
Routes never write credential/session persistence directly or accept client role, account, center, membership, or session identity as authorization.
Existing Telegram/Google login and invitation flows remain available and behaviorally unchanged.
verification_targets: FT-001-AC-011 / REQ-001 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/authentication-transport.md#session-issuance-and-revocation: disposable pre-created credential plus HTTP/SSR probes prove normalized-email success, exact Admin actor and /admin redirect, existing foundation_session cookie attributes, logout/revocation denial, and no direct route persistence.

FT-001-AC-011 / REQ-001 / .memory-bank/contracts/access-control.md#binding-and-session-rules: unknown email and wrong password return the same status/body and issue no session; instrumentation/source probe confirms scrypt plus timingSafeEqual and no externally observable account-existence branch.

.memory-bank/states/lifecycle-map.md#access-and-membership: successful password verification is the only new session issuance predecessor and the existing issued-to-revoked lifecycle remains unchanged.
Existing FT-001 provider login/invitation regression: focused Telegram/Google login/invitation tests remain green without deleting or changing provider routes.
deployment.md: browser instructions use the normalized email/password form and existing Admin flow without documenting password literals or new secret transport.
